primary_topics: Policy analysis of President GMA's options after her last SONA (July 27, 2009), published July 30, 2009 -- structured as three major option tracks: step down, extend reign, or prevent

Option 1 -- Step down: exit gracefully with a legacy-oriented SONA (strong economy, 33-quarter growth, doubled GDP); protect back via institutional control; choose a viable presidential candidate or run for VP or Congress

Option 2 -- Extend reign: Cha-cha via three routes (no time for any of them); martial law (only for invasion/rebellion, 60 days, Congress can revoke, SC reviews factual basis); emergency rule (no constitutional authority)
Option 3 -- Preventions: HOPE elections; vigilant people and media; People Power; CBCP; Twitter revolt; full-scale revolution
sub_topics: GMA's SONA bites (economic achievements cited): 'The state of our nation is a strong economy. Our reforms gave us the resources to protect our people... Since 2001 our economy posted uninterrupted growth for 33 quarters; more than double its size from $76 billion to $186 billion. The average GDP growth from 2001 to the first quarter of 2009 is the highest in 43 years. I never expressed the desire to extend myself beyond my term. I accepted the invitation of President Obama to be the first Southeast Asian leader to meet him at the White House later this week.'

Protecting back: 'strengthen hold on the House of Representatives, Supreme Court and Sandiganbayan, Ombudsman, Commission on Elections, and Military. Choose a viable presidential candidate who would shield her; run for vice-president and team up with Noli or Erap; run for a congressional seat in Pampanga.'

Cha-cha routes: peoples initiative (for simple amendments only, not complicated revisions); constituent assembly (three-fourths vote of all members of Congress); constitutional convention (no more time before elections)

Martial law: 'to quell invasion or rebellion for 60 days only; may be revoked, shortened or extended by majority vote of all members of Congress; SC can pass upon the sufficiency of the factual basis; SC must decide within 30 days'
Emergency rule: 'no constitutional authority; no international backing; our people will rebel against it; even the military may not support it'

Holdover: 'no election due to man-made or natural causes; no proclamation due to election held but no winner chosen due to automation problems; succession to the presidency via VP, Senate President, Speaker'

stances.claim: Emergency rule has no constitutional authority, no international backing, and would face domestic rebellion -- 'even the military may not support it.' This is CJP's most categorical dismissal of a GMA option, based on constitutional analysis rather than political preference.
stances.rhetorical_move: triple-no argument: no constitutional authority + no international backing + domestic rebellion as the three-pronged dismissal of emergency rule

stances.claim: The cleanest and most credible option for GMA is Option 1: exit gracefully with a strong economy legacy narrative, protect her back institutionally, and work through a viable successor candidate. The other options (Cha-cha, martial law, emergency rule, holdover) all face serious constitutional, legal or political obstacles.
stances.rhetorical_move: Option-1-as-cleanest by elimination: the other options' enumerated obstacles make Option 1 the de facto best choice
stances.confidence: asserted as the implicit governing analytical conclusion

notable_anecdotes: GMA's Obama White House visit as the exit narrative: at the very end of her SONA, GMA noted 'I never expressed the desire to extend myself beyond my term. I accepted the invitation of President Obama to be the first Southeast Asian leader to meet him at the White House later this week.' -- framing her legacy as globally recognized.

Twitter revolt as a prevention option: listed alongside People Power, CBCP and full-scale revolution as a way to prevent an unconstitutional extension -- one of the earliest mentions of Twitter as a political tool in the corpus.

Emergency rule's triple dismissal: 'no constitutional authority; no international backing; our people will rebel against it; even the military may not support it' -- four separate reasons in one sentence.

one_paragraph_summary: Published July 30, 2009 as a policy analysis of President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo's options after her last SONA (July 27, 2009), this document by CJP presents three tracks. Option 1 -- Step down: exit gracefully with a legacy narrative (strong economy, 33-quarter uninterrupted growth, GDP doubled from $76B to $186B, 'highest average GDP growth in 43 years,' imminent White House visit as first Southeast Asian leader to meet Obama); protect institutional back (House, SC, Sandiganbayan, Ombudsman, Comelec, Military); choose a viable presidential candidate or run for VP (with Noli or Erap) or for a Pampanga congressional seat. Option 2 -- Extend reign as PM/President: (a) Cha-cha via people's initiative (for simple amendments only, not revisions), constituent assembly (three-fourths of all Congress), or con-con (no more time before elections); (b) martial law (only for invasion/rebellion; 60 days only; Congress can revoke; SC reviews factual basis within 30 days); (c) emergency rule -- 'no constitutional authority; no international backing; our people will rebel against it; even the military may not support it'; (d) holdover -- 'not expressly provided by the Constitution but supported by jurisprudence.' Option 3 -- Preventions: HOPE elections; vigilant people and media; People Power; CBCP; Twitter revolt; full-scale revolution. (Note: this is a companion to SE103's Automation or Confusion analysis from April 2010.)
